Moderator:  
Ladies and gentlemen, good day, and welcome to Sri Lotus Developers and Realty Limited’s 
Q2 FY27 Earnings Conference Call. Before we begin, I would like to remind participants that 
this conference call may contain forward-looking statements about the company, which are 
based on the beliefs, opinions, and expectations of the company as on date of this call. These 
statements are not guarantee of future performance and involve risks and uncertainties that are 
difficult to predict.  
 
As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode, and there will be an 
opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need assistance 
during the conference call, please signal an operator by pressing star then zero on your touchtone 
phone. Please note that this conference is being recorded.  
 
With this, I now hand the conference over to Mr. Anand Pandit, Managing Director and 
Chairman of Sri Lotus Developers and Realty Limited. Thank you, and over to you, sir. 
Anand Pandit: 
Good morning, everyone, and a very warm welcome to the Q2 and H1 FY27 Earnings Call of 
Sri Lotus Developers and Realty Limited. Joining me today are our CEO, Mr. Sanjay Kumar 
Jain; our CFO, Mr. Rakesh Gupta; and our Investor Relations Advisors from SGA. Our investor 
presentation has been uploaded to the stock exchanges and our website, and we hope you have 
had a chance to go through it.  
 
Let me begin with a brief update on the real estate market. Mumbai remains India’s largest 
housing market, with sales in the first nine months of calendar 2026 at their highest since 2018, 
and the luxury segment continues to lead. In the first half of the calendar year, sales of homes 
priced above INR10 crores reached a record of over INR18,500 crores, while prime residential 
prices rose 6.2% year-on-year, more than twice the global average.  
 
Demand is driven largely by end users upgrading to larger homes in better locations, while scarce 
land in prime micromarkets makes redevelopment the principal route to new supply, precisely 
where Lotus has built its capability.  
 
Before I begin with the business update, a word on interest rates. Earlier this month, RBI raised 
the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.5%, its first increase since early 2023. While this is likely 
to weigh on affordable and mid-income housing, the luxury segment is far less sensitive to 
borrowing costs. Our buyers rely far less on home loans and buy for long-term value and 
lifestyle. We, therefore, do not expect it to materially alter demand in the micromarkets we 
operate in.  
 
Turning to our performance, Q2 FY27 completes a strong first half for Lotus. Delighted to share 
that we recorded pre-sales for the quarter at INR470 crores, up 83% year-on-year. For H1 FY27, 
pre-sales stood at INR879 crores, up 176% year-on-year.  
 
Our growth has not come at the cost of profitability. In Q2, total revenue rose 53% year-on-year 
to INR269 crores. EBITDA more than doubled to INR107 crores, with margins expanding to 
39.9%.

For the first half, revenue stood at INR401 crores, up 69%, EBITDA at INR155 crores, up 95%, 
and PAT at INR134 crores, up 86% at an improved PAT margin of 33.5%.  
 
Collections stood at INR60 crores for the quarter and INR209 crores for the first half. Collections 
in our business are linked to construction milestones and can vary from quarter-to-quarter. As 
our ongoing projects progress and recent launches reach their billing milestones, we expect 
collections to pick up over the coming quarters.  
 
Our recent launches continue to perform well. Lotus Trident in Andheri West, our luxury 
commercial offering, has been a standout performer, contributing pre-sales of INR178 crores in 
its first full quarter since its launch at the end of June. Its success shows how well the Lotus 
brand travels beyond ultra-luxury residential into luxury commercial real estate.  
 
We also made significant progress on business development during the quarter. Three new 
projects added, Lotus Impressa at Shivaji Park in Dadar West, Lotus Stellar in Versova, and 
Lotus Supremus in Juhu, which adds INR2,700 to INR2,800 crores of GDV to existing GDV 
pipeline. 
These additions deepen our presence in Juhu and Versova, where we have a strong track record, 
and extend our footprint to Shivaji Park, one of Central Mumbai’s most established residential 
neighborhoods. With these additions, our ongoing and upcoming pipeline now comprises 24 
projects with an aggregate GDV of approximately INR20,000 crores, of which 19 are 
redevelopment-led.  
 
Looking ahead, we are well-prepared for the second half. We plan to launch four projects, Lotus 
Aurelia, Lotus Sky Plaza, Lotus Portofino, and Lotus Odyssey, with a combined estimated GDV 
of INR3,500 to INR4,000 crores. 
Together with the momentum from our recent launches and a growing pipeline, we remain 
confident of delivering our FY27 guideline of pre-sales in the range of INR1,800 crores to 
INR2,000 crores, along with revenue and PAT growth of 55% to 60% over FY26 levels. We 
also remain confident of sustaining strong profitability, with EBITDA and PAT margin expected 
at 35% to 40% and 25% to 30%, respectively.  
 
Behind these numbers is a simple operating philosophy. We select projects on the strength of 
their location and margins, not their scale, and we oversee every stage of the development 
ourselves, from design and construction to sales and customer engagement. 
This is what enables us to deliver consistently strong margins, and the credibility we have built 
with housing societies and development partners continues to open up new redevelopment 
opportunities for us, as reflected in the 3 additions in this quarter.  
 
With that, I will now hand over the call to Mr. Sanjay Kumar Jain, our CEO, to take you through 
the financial highlights in more detail. Thank you.

Sanjay Kumar Jain: 
Thank you, Anand sir. Good morning, everyone. Let me now take you through our financial 
performance for Q2 and H1 FY27, which reflects strong business momentum, significant growth 
in profitability, and continued progress in expanding our development portfolio.  
 
Let me begin with our business performance and growth outlook. Lotus Trident in Andheri West 
delivered pre-sales of INR178 crores in Q2, marking its first full quarter since launch. Lotus 
Aquaria in Prabhadevi continued to witness healthy inquiry level. During the quarter, we further 
strengthened our development pipeline by adding three new projects at Shivaji Park, Dadar 
West; second in Versova; and in Juhu. 
Together, these additions represent an estimated GDV of INR2,700 crores approximately. 
Looking ahead, we plan to launch four projects in H2 FY27: Lotus Sky Plaza, Lotus Portofino, 
Lotus Aurelia, and Lotus Odyssey, which have a combined estimated GDV of INR3,500 crores 
to INR4,000 crores. These additions provide us with a strong pipeline of future opportunity and 
reinforce our focus on expanding our portfolio and creating long-term value.  
Coming to our financial performance, Q2 FY27 delivered strong growth across our key financial 
parameters. Pre-sales grew 83% year-on-year to INR470 crores, compared with INR257 crores 
in corresponding quarter last year. 
Total revenue increased 53% to INR269 crores, while EBITDA more than doubled, growing 
113% to INR107 crores from INR50 crores. Our EBITDA margin remained healthy at 39.90%. 
Profit after tax grew 91% to INR89 crores, compared with INR46 crores in Q2 FY26. The 
combination of strong revenue growth, substantial EBITDA expansion, and higher profitability 
demonstrates the strength of our operating performance. 
Turning to H1 FY27, our performance reflects an even stronger growth trajectory. Pre-sales 
increased 176% year-on-year to INR879 crores, compared with INR319 crores in H1 FY26. 
Total revenue grew 69% to INR401 crores, EBITDA increased 95% to INR155 crores, with a 
healthy margin of 38.80%. 
Profit after tax rose 86% to INR134 crores, compared with INR72 crores in corresponding period 
last year. Overall, these numbers demonstrate strong momentum across sales, revenue, and 
profitability, providing a solid foundation for the next phase of our growth.  
Moving to our balance sheet, maintaining financial strength and flexibility remained a key 
priority. As of 30th September 2026, we had a net cash position of INR494 crores. This provides 
us with the financial flexibility to fund our ongoing projects, support upcoming launches, and 
pursue new development opportunity, while maintaining a disciplined capital structure. In 
addition, our estimated project-level surplus stands at approximately INR9,500 crores over the 
development cycle of our portfolio. 
This represents significant potential value from our projects, subject to the project execution, 
realization, cost, and other relevant assumptions. It is important to distinguish this projected 
project-level surplus from our current cash balance or accounting profits.

On capital deployment, we remain committed to disciplined and transparent utilization of funds. 
We raised approximately INR792 crores through the fresh issue of our IPO, with net proceeds 
of approximately INR732 crores after issue expenses, of which INR550 crores earmarked for 
our subsidiary for the Amalfi, Arcadian, and Varun. INR305 crores had been deployed as on 
30th September 2026. We remain on track with our planned utilization schedule. 
To conclude, H1 FY27 has been a strong period for the company. We have delivered 176% 
growth in pre-sales, nearly doubled our EBITDA, significantly increased our profitability, and 
maintained a net cash position. With four planned project launches in H2 FY27, a strengthened 
development pipeline, a disciplined approach to capital deployment, we are focused on 
sustaining our growth momentum, executing our projects efficiently, and delivering long-term 
value for our shareholders. With that, I would like to open the floor for questions. Thank you.
